raw_glosses: (countable, uncountable, informal) Cola-based soft drink; (in particular) Coca-Cola.

examples.text: The waiter came up, and I ordered a Coke for her—she didn't drink—and a Scotch and soda for myself, but the sonuvabitch wouldn't bring me one, so I had a Coke, too.
examples.ref: 1951 July 16, J[erome] D[avid] Salinger, The Catcher in the Rye, Boston, Mass.: Little, Brown and Company, →OCLC, page 168:

examples.text: 'You have a coke and I'll have a beer and we can talk business.'
examples.ref: 1958, Franklin Martin, “The Trouble with Mrs. Benton”, in Venus, volume 1, number 1, Garden of Eve Publications, page 16:

raw_glosses: (countable, informal) A bottle, glass or can of Coca-Cola or a cola-based soft drink.
glosses: A bottle, glass or can of Coca-Cola or a cola-based soft drink.

raw_glosses: (US, especially Southern US, informal, genericized trademark) Any soft drink, regardless of type.
glosses: Any soft drink, regardless of type.
